title: Probability bounds on trajectory-level exceedances of quantum speed limits under continuous-measurement feedback
abstract: We investigate the probability that a conditioned quantum trajectory exceeds an ensemble-derived quantum speed limit (QSL) velocity under continuous measurement-based feedback. Using the finite-time average fidelity velocity, we derive an upper bound on the exceedance probability in terms of its mean and variance. We further obtain state-independent bounds from uniform constraints on the fidelity drift and diffusion, including an exponential concentration bound. For a feedback-controlled qubit, we derive explicit model-specific bounds and show that they are nontrivial in a short-time regime. We also identify a finite-time regime in which the exceedance probability vanishes exactly due to the restricted support of the conditioned dynamics. Monte Carlo simulations confirm the analytical bounds and illustrate their tightness.
summary: This paper develops rigorous analytical upper bounds for the probability that a quantum system's evolution, governed by continuous measurement feedback, exceeds its theoretical Quantum Speed Limit. Using the fidelity dynamics, the authors derive state-independent and model-specific bounds, demonstrating that the probability can vanish entirely in certain short-time regimes. This provides a quantitative measure of how well feedback control adheres to fundamental quantum speed constraints.
main_problem: The paper derives analytical upper bounds on the probability that a quantum trajectory, conditioned by continuous measurement feedback, exceeds a theoretically derived Quantum Speed Limit (QSL) velocity.
main_result: The probability bound is established using two primary methods—a variance-based bound and an exponential concentration bound—and a zero-probability regime is identified for sufficiently short times.
method: The analysis employs stochastic master equations (SME) for the conditioned state and applies concentration inequalities (like Cantelli's) to the finite-time average fidelity velocity.
model_or_system: The study analyzes general open quantum systems undergoing continuous measurement and feedback control, with a detailed application to a feedback-controlled qubit stabilization model.
key_observables: Finite-time average fidelity velocity ($v_c$), Quantum Speed Limit velocity ($v_{QSL}$), and the exceedance probability $	ext{Pr}[v_c \geq v_{QSL}]$.
important_parameters: Measurement strength ($\kappa$), feedback parameter ($\alpha$), and the time scale ($	au$).
main_assumptions: The general bounds rely on assuming uniform bounds on the drift and diffusion coefficients of the fidelity process; model-specific bounds use purity and Bloch dynamics geometry.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the analytical bounds, comparing the derived $P_C$ and $P_E$ bounds, and showing the regime where the exceedance probability vanishes.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general framework using the SME and defines the QSL and exceedance velocity. It then derives general state-independent bounds, followed by a detailed application to the qubit model to derive tighter, model-specific bounds, concluding with an analysis of the zero-probability regime.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to quantify the deviation of actual quantum evolution from theoretical speed limits under realistic, noisy, and controlled measurement processes, which is crucial for quantum control theory.
